text:
It hails so much, enough for me to remember

and increase the pearls

I have gathered from the very snout

of every storm.


Let this rain not dry up.

Unless I were granted

to fall now for it, or they buried me

wet in the water

that would spring from all fires.


How far will this rain reach me?

I fear some flank of mine will remain dry;

I fear it will go away without having tested me

in the droughts of incredible vocal cords,

through which,

to give harmony,

one must always climb-never descend!

Do we not perhaps climb downward?


Sing, rain, on the coast still without sea!

translation.title: Trilce: Poem LXXVII - It Hails So Much, Enough for Me to Remember
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's reversals: rain from fire, climbing downward, and a coast without sea.
